Class CharReader

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.io.CharReader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class CharReader extends Object implements Closeable
Reads a stream of characters: lines, runs of characters, lookahead and search, for reading text formats.

A reader holds a buffer, and reads from its stream only when a call needs characters that aren't buffered yet, taking what the stream has at hand: it never waits for more characters than the call needs.

Counts and offsets are in chars. The methods that test characters with a predicate give it code points, joining surrogate pairs, so that the methods of Character that take an int, such as Character.isWhitespace(int), work on every character.

When the stream ends before a read method has all the characters it needs, the method throws EOFException and leaves the reader at the end of the stream. The lookahead methods, request(int), require(int), exhausted(), peek(), startsWith(CharSequence) and the indexOf methods, never consume anything. 

// key = value lines, with # comments
while (!in.exhausted()) {
    in.skipWhile(Character::isWhitespace);
    if (in.startsWith("#")) {
        in.readLine(MAX_LINE);
        continue;
    }
    var key = in.readWhile(c -> c != '=' && !Character.isWhitespace(c), MAX_KEY);
    in.skipWhile(c -> c == ' ' || c == '\t');
    if (in.peek() != '=') {
        throw new IOException("expected '=' after " + key);
    }
    in.skip(1);
    var value = in.readLine(MAX_LINE).orElse("").strip();
}

A reader owns its stream: close() closes it, and any other call that needs the stream after that throws IOException. A reader is not safe for use by several threads at once.

Since:
0.1.3

      public Optional<String> readLine(int maxLength) throws IOException
      Reads a line. A line ends with a line feed (\n), a carriage return (\r), a carriage return followed by a line feed, or the end of the stream, as for BufferedReader.readLine().
      Parameters:
      maxLength - the number of characters the line may have, at most, its terminator excluded
      Returns:
      the line, without its terminator, or an empty optional at the end of the stream
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxLength is negative
      IOException - if the line has more than maxLength characters, in which case nothing is consumed, or if the stream cannot be read

    • readWhile

      public String readWhile(IntPredicate test, int maxLength) throws IOException
      Reads the code points that pass a test, up to the first that doesn't, a length limit or the end of the stream. Reaching the limit is not an error: peek() or another lookahead tells whether the run goes on.
      Parameters:
      test - the test that the code points to read pass
      maxLength - the number of characters to read, at most; a surrogate pair that would exceed it is not read
      Returns:
      the characters read, which may be none
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxLength is negative
      IOException - if the stream cannot be read
